summary_en: Dividend policy revised to target 40% consolidated payout ratio, replacing prior framework tied to 4% yield threshold. FY2026 year-end dividend raised to 16 yen per share from prior forecast of 10 yen, combining with interim dividend of 10 yen for annual payout of 26 yen (40.6% payout ratio).
title_en: Notice of Change in Dividend Policy (Target Consolidated Payout Ratio of Approximately 40%) and Revision of Year-End Dividend Forecast (Dividend Increase)
translation_en_brief:
A.D.Works Group announced a revision to its dividend policy effective from the fiscal year ended December 2026. The company is shifting from a previous framework that targeted a minimum 4% dividend yield while maintaining payout ratio below 50%, to a new policy targeting a consolidated payout ratio of approximately 40%. The company cited the need to align dividend decisions with consolidated earnings rather than stock price movements, which fluctuate due to factors unrelated to business performance, thereby enhancing predictability for shareholders and improving consistency with capital allocation principles.

Concurrently, the company raised its year-end dividend forecast for FY2026 to 16 yen per share, an increase of 6 yen from the prior guidance of 10 yen announced on August 6, 2026. Combined with the interim dividend of 10 yen already paid, the total annual dividend is now expected to reach 26 yen per share, representing a consolidated payout ratio of 40.6% based on projected earnings per share of 64.01 yen. This compares to a payout ratio of 23.4% in the prior fiscal year ended December 2025.

The policy change reflects the company's strategic framework articulated in its third medium-term management plan, scheduled for announcement in February 2027, which will detail the company's comprehensive capital allocation approach balancing growth investment, financial soundness, and shareholder returns.
